prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, a new travel mood is becoming clearer in Japan.

Young travelers, especially young men, are showing a wish to travel at their own pace. They want more time for personal interests, not just a busy list of famous places.

Several surveys point in this direction. Among men aged 29 and under, about one in four preferred solo travel, and a similar share preferred travel that helps them enjoy a hobby more deeply.

Another survey asked Japanese people aged 19 to 25 about overseas tours. About 90% said they wanted free time during the tour. Of these, about 80% wanted half a day or more.

There is also a strong wish for longer holidays. When people were asked what they would do if they had one month off, the most common answer was a trip of about one week.

But here is the surprising part.

The trips people actually plan are still short. In an autumn survey, people planning a trip expected to stay just under two nights on average. The middle answer was two nights.

Japan’s Tourism White Paper also says that making stays longer is still an important policy task.

So, Japan has not already moved from sightseeing to long stays. Instead, two things are happening at the same time. The wish for a slower, more personal trip is becoming clearer. But the time people spend away is still limited.

【Point One】
A short trip is not automatically a tightly packed trip. A traveler may still want half a day for a hobby or personal interest. The early change may be about who controls the schedule, not the number of nights. This helps explain why a slower travel style can appear before longer holidays become common.

【Point Two】
Young travelers do not all want the same thing. For men under 30, about 25% preferred solo travel, and a similar share preferred hobby-focused travel. For women in the same age group, visiting famous tourist sites was still high at about 45%. The key point is coexistence, not replacement. Tourism may need both personal choices and landmark routes.

point_one.reasoning: 滞在日数が短くても、予定を詰め込まず趣味や個人的関心に時間を使う旅行は可能だという区別を示している。これは、長期休暇の普及前に旅行スタイルの変化が表れる理由を具体的に説明しており、本文の単なる言い換えではない。

point_two.reasoning: 男性のソロ・趣味重視志向と、女性では有名観光地志向がなお強いという性別差を追加し、旅行需要が一方向に置き換わるのではなく併存すると示している。観光業が個人向けの自由時間と定番観光ルートの両方を用意すべきだという具体的な示唆もある。
